subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): add AES-256-GCM encryption for persisted auth secrets

question: Which key-custody and recovery model should protect SQLite auth-profile credentials, and must it cover other credential stores before this format merges?
rationale: The line-level data-preservation defect is clear, but permanent key management, unattended startup, recovery, rotation, and cross-store scope require explicit security and product intent.

options.title: Design canonical encrypted storage
options.body: Define keychain or passphrase custody with doctor migration, recovery, rotation, and upgrade proof before merging this format.

options.title: Approve narrow environment-key mode
options.body: Accept an auth-profile-only expert mode with explicit lockout semantics after correcting the missing-key defect.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause this implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43794 resolves the broader credential-protection direction.

recommendation.title: Design canonical encrypted storage
recommendation.body: Define keychain or passphrase custody with doctor migration, recovery, rotation, and upgrade proof before merging this format.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue's history review identifies vincentkoc as the strongest available owner for auth-store sealing and credential-security direction.
